Data Labeling for Machine Learning Engineers: Project-Based Curriculum and Data-Centric Competitions

paper.aaai.26886

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at AAAI-37-13-26886-26658-captured-2026-11-10. Curriculum/project-round content covers annotation pipeline engineering and quality/budget/time conditions; the industrial secrecy and prerequisite limitations prevent a generalized learning-effect claim. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The course requires programming and ML/deep-learning preparation; confidential business algorithms and the need to train and coordinate practitioner lecturers constrain transfer of the approach.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The 2021 curriculum organized data labeling into three project rounds focused on annotation quality, budget constraints, and changing data over time; students collected data for a specified model.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

For third-year respondents, reported career usefulness rose from 3.16 in 2020 to 3.8 in 2021 on a 1–5 survey scale; the paper reports 35 third-year respondents and also reports mixed fourth-year feedback.
